clue.text: Altercation: then to meet

parts.note: a run-in is a quarrel or clash with someone

explanation.surface: A row breaks out, and then the two parties meet.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to encounter them by chance, an idiom for meeting.

clue.text: Brush off and polish again?

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: Brushing something down and shining it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a curt refusal, giving someone the brush-off.

clue.text: As an author, did he deliver for William the Conqueror?

definitions.text: As an author, did he deliver for William the Conqueror?

parts.words: As an author, did he deliver for William the Conqueror?
parts.note: read whimsically, a postman serving the invader of 1066 would be the conqueror's own letter-carrier; the real figure is an American novelist

explanation.surface: Was a famous writer a postman for William the Conqueror?
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote The Naked and the Dead; his name splits into a Conqueror's people and a postman.

clue.text: Midget PC's rank?

parts.note: a tiny police constable is barely a policeman at all, and the phrase also means of poor quality, rank

explanation.surface: What grade is a very small police officer?
explanation.walkthrough: PC is a British police constable; 'not much cop' is British slang for not very good.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for something of little worth, like a small police officer is hardly a full one.

clue.text: Milton's time-consuming instrument

definitions.note: the clue's 's is short for is, so the definition is the name alone

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the instrument swallows the letter

parts.note: the oboe is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: Milton's instrument takes a long time to play.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the poet John Milton: Milton Obote was the first prime minister and later president of Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ugandan leader's forename was Milton, so his surname completes the name.

clue.text: Gun sure to grab attention

indicators.note: one word seizing another holds it inside, so these letters take in the next piece

parts.note: firm means certain or sure
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A firearm is a sure way to make people pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is a portable weapon firing bullets, the commonest kind of firearm.

clue.text: Is business contract his, having crossed the Channel?

indicators.note: a man who has crossed over is now inside the country beyond

parts.note: France lies across the English Channel from Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a man's trading deal still valid once he moves to France?
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence contract letting someone trade under another firm's brand.

clue.text: Jelly served up, music to Indian ears?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: Dessert jelly is brought to the table, a delight to an Indian diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Lorry passing round one way, being creative

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the lorry surrounds these letters

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck
I is the Roman numeral one
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A lorry driving round a one-way system shows imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative people have artistic talent, the two being near synonyms.

clue.text: Partners in joint heading for lavatory, entertaining itinerant

indicators.note: the partners sit inside the joint

parts.note: a mitre is a corner joint in woodwork
North and South are partners in bridge

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Partners in a pub head off to the toilet while a wandering singer entertains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like the container signal, but it belongs in the definition: an itinerant who entertains.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval minstrel was a travelling singer and musician.

clue.text: Phone people about vessel like the Cutty Sark, sadly

indicators.note: one piece placed around another, so the phone company's letters surround the vessel

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: Telephone engineers fussing over a famous old sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cutty Sark is a preserved tea clipper in Greenwich, London, badly damaged by fire in 2007, hence 'sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship was gutted by fire in 2007, so being fire-damaged was its sad fate.

clue.text: Inside out, sounded an animal

indicators.note: the next piece is set within the word that follows, so the bell's sound goes into out

parts.note: taken as written
a bell that sounded rang
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal's call echoes through, turned inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside out' reads as a phrase, but 'Inside' is the container signal and 'out' is the word cut open.
explanation.definitionFit: The great red-haired ape of Borneo and Sumatra is one particular animal.

clue.text: All furious about trade union leaders involved in criminal's unfortunate release

indicators.note: the built group is wrapped up inside the criminal's word

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the union initials
a furious state is wild and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Union officials lose their temper over a criminal's embarrassing escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' gives LAL; 'release' looks like a prisoner's freedom, given 'criminal', but the surface conceals a rude joke about wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing wind is a release of gas, unfortunate when it happens in company.

clue.text: Listen, taking a couple of seconds during exercise

indicators.note: something occurring during another sits within it, so the seconds go inside

parts.note: PT is physical training

indicators.note: two copies of the following letter are wanted

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A coach tells a class to pay attention for a moment mid-workout.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered call to catch someone's attention works as a hushed request to listen.

clue.text: Old bags criticise love in the grip of birds?

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: love is placed inside the claws

parts.note: talons are the claws birds of prey grip with
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Elderly women are slated while birds of prey hold them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bags' suggests unkind words for women; here bags are trousers, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloons are old-fashioned baggy trousers, and bags is slang for trousers.

clue.text: Isolates hip in order to admit for treatment

indicators.note: putting letters into order means rearranging them, so these are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor separates a patient with a bad hip so they can be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital admission for medical care is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Just tell me what to do when wine tasting?

definitions.meaning: an impatient urge to say something frankly

definitions.text: what to do when wine tasting?
definitions.meaning: tasters spit the wine out rather than swallowing it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges blunt speech, and literally describes expelling a mouthful of wine.

clue.text: Temple on this austere policy, following princess

indicators.note: the policy comes after the princess

parts.note: Di was Diana, Princess of Wales
strict means severe or austere
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A temple runs a stern regime after a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Temple is a station on the London Underground's District line, not a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Underground station at Temple lies on this route.

clue.text: Endless worry in Accident & Emergency's opening

indicators.note: the shortened worry sits inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: A and E is the hospital emergency department

indicators.note: with no end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to perturb is to worry

explanation.surface: Constant anxiety inside a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of PERTURB, leaving PERTUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, an opening.

clue.text: Naughty child, six, feeding rat, gets rash

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: food goes into a mouth, so six is put inside the rat

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A naughty six-year-old feeds a rat and ends up with a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' seems to be the skin complaint, but it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting without forethought, the same as failing to provide for the future.

clue.text: See 2
Attempt to cut tree, climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from the bottom up
the attempt cuts into the tree, going inside it

parts.note: the elm is a tree
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to fell a tree with a climbing plant around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' gives ELTRYM, which 'climbing' turns upwards; 'climbing plant' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen flowering shrub, a plant.

clue.text: Wrong to run backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong, such as negligence, for which damages may be sought.

clue.text: Is subversive group infiltrating a lot of different things?

indicators.note: agents infiltrating something get inside it, so these pieces go within

parts.note: many means a lot
taken as written
a cell is a small group of activists or spies

explanation.surface: Is a revolutionary cell getting into all sorts of organisations?
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of various different items.

clue.text: Item of jewellery making brief appearance

definitions.meaning: a brooch carved in relief with a profile
a small role played by a famous actor

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery shows up briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a relief-carved gem and a celebrity's short film role.

clue.text: See 16
Single woman of peace I class as dressed for battle, perhaps?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nun is a religious woman, a woman of peace
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pacifist nun is oddly cast as someone in military dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' because a uniform need not be military: soldiers in uniform are only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in uniform describes soldiers kitted out for duty, battle being one possibility.

clue.text: Duck left in rain, baby bird

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the word for rain

parts.note: the wet means rainy weather

explanation.surface: A duck stranded in the rain beside a chick.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a baby bird, the suffix marking a little one.

clue.text: Adverb present among rubbish

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
here means present, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson finds an adverb lurking in a pile of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word meaning 'at that place', used to modify verbs, so an adverb.

clue.text: Jack's off work to attend to clock

indicators.note: a letter that is off has gone, so it is taken away

parts.note: a job is a piece of work
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
to serve someone is to attend to them

explanation.surface: Jack skips work to see to a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' looks like the timepiece but is the slang verb meaning to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to clock someone is to notice or spot them.
